text:
Priya (oncall): Heads-up — starting ~09:00 UTC east1 GPU pools are failing fast during provisioning, autoscaler shows repeated 502s from the node-provisioner. Not all requests, but enough to exceed healthy threshold :rotating_light:
InfraBot: [ALERT] east1-gpu-pool: provisioning_latency_high (90th=36s) — triggered 1823455998
Diego: Copy. Is this affecting both p3 and a10 pools or just the a10 burst ones?
Priya (oncall): Mostly the a10-burst and the small lower-priority pools. p3 reserved looks ok so far.
Sam L.: Any quick mitigation? Can we shift traffic away from a10 pools to reserved capacity?
Maya - SRE Lead: We can do an automated route policy change, but need a quick customer-facing note first. If we shift, costs will jump for burst customers and some low-priority jobs will queue.
Anya - Support: I'm already seeing two open tickets from customers with timeouts. Need ETA to include in replies.
Diego: Repro logs from provisioner:
```
ERROR provisioning: createInstance timeout=30s pool=a10-burst id=pool-78f
http status=502 body="driver-init-failed"
call_trace: provisioner.assign -> driver.create
```
Priya (oncall): Thanks. Root cause likely a GPU driver rollout that landed in the region's host image. We detected a docker shim regression in the new image. Rolling back is in progress but could take ~20-40m.
Maya - SRE Lead: Rolling rollback now (command run):
```
infractl images rollback --region east1 --image-tag stable-2026-03-17 --pools a10-burst
```
Maya - SRE Lead: ETA for rollback to finish across nodes ~ 25m, then we need to drain and reprovision nodes which is another 10-20m for the larger pools.
Anya - Support: Draft statuspage blurb for review:
"We are investigating increased provisioning failures in east1 causing delayed or failed instance allocations for burst GPU pools. We are performing a rollback of a recent host image and expect improved provisioning within 30-45 minutes. We will post updates and impacted customer guidance shortly."
Priya (oncall): Edit suggestion: call out that hosted inference endpoints should remain serving on pinned models, but new dedicated pool provisioning and some autoscale bursts may fail. Also include mitigation steps for customers (e.g., retry backoff, use reserved capacity).
Sam L.: +1 to calling out reserved capacity. Also add: customers on Dedicated might see tail latency spikes if we shift traffic to fewer nodes.
Diego: Operational note: triggering temporary traffic shift rule for requests tagged burst=true to fallback to region us-central1 and to an a10-compatible variant. Command:
```
routeset apply --selector "tag:burst=true and region:east1" --fallback region=us-central1 model_variant=a10-compatible --duration 60m
```
Maya - SRE Lead: Before we apply, we need support author's signoff for customer notification language. Anya, can you confirm?
Anya - Support: Confirmed. I'll post the status update and start proactive messages to impacted customers with the suggested workaround. Suggested SLA note appended: "We are treating this as a degradation incident; we will not count provisioning failures toward uptime for customers using burst pools while rollback completes."
Priya (oncall): Applying traffic shift in 2m. Will annotate all changes in the incident runbook.
InfraBot: [ACTION] routeset apply scheduled by Priya at 1823456232: id=rs-91b, selector="tag:burst=true and region:east1" fallback=us-central1 duration=60m
Diego: After rollback completes, let's run a canary reprovision against a small subset: `provisioner.test --pool a10-burst --count 4` and check kv-cache and driver logs.
Maya - SRE Lead: Agreed. Also add a cost note in the incident: shifting burst traffic to other regions may incur cross-region egress and higher per-token GPU billing. I'll capture expected cost delta for customers and internal billing.
Anya - Support: Posting status now. Copy of message to customers:
"Status: Partial provisioning failures in east1 for burst GPU pools. We are rolling back a recent host image and temporarily routing burst requests to us-central1. Expected mitigation within 30–45 minutes. Impact: delayed provisioning for new dedicated/burst instances; live hosted inference for pinned models should remain available. If you require guaranteed capacity, please contact support to enable reserved capacity or to migrate."
:envelope_with_arrow: sending to affected customers via support batch-1
Priya (oncall): Update: rollback started; first nodes reporting stable at 1823456350. Continuing rollout.
Sam L.: Noted. Keep the traffic shift in place until we see three consecutive successful provision attempts in east1 canary.
Maya - SRE Lead: Canary run passed first set at 1823456520 (4/4 provisioned). Waiting 1 more cycle.
Priya (oncall): Final update: rollback complete and canary passed. Reverting route fallback now and posting final status update. Total incident duration ~10m from detection to full resolution for core pools; burst provisioning impact lasted ~40m for some customers.
Anya - Support: Final customer note queued and sent. No escalations to execs. Closing incident after postmortem schedule tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
